reason: Prepare the new membrane needed for cell growth and division.
expectation: Phospholipids and proteins should form membrane material; I’m unsure how it will be incorporated into the cell.

alternatives.reason: Copying DNA is also essential, but I’ll prepare the membrane first.

effect: The vesicles provide a membrane supply, and the next goal is to use it to enlarge the cell.
reaction: The ER and Golgi inset suggests where the vesicles come from, though their role is not explained.
reason: Use the new membrane supply to address the revealed growth goal.
expectation: The vesicles will add membrane to the growing cell, probably by fusing with its surface.

alternatives.reason: Copying DNA is also a goal, but I’ll follow the membrane preparation through first.

effect: Vesicle fusion enlarged the cell, but its nuclear DNA still needs copying.
reaction: The fusion inset made the membrane addition clear.
reason: Copy the nuclear DNA so each eventual daughter can receive a complete genome.
expectation: The cell will use the nucleotides to duplicate its nuclear DNA.

alternatives.reason: Building the spindle is also necessary, but I’ll copy the DNA first.

effect: The nuclear DNA is copied, and the next goal is to use a spindle to form two daughter nuclei.
reaction: The joined sister chromatids make the copied chromosomes visible, though S phase is not explained here.
reason: Build the spindle needed for the new goal; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Proteins and duplicated centrosomes will form a spindle that can move chromosomes.

effect: The spindle is assembled after DNA copying, but chromosomes have not yet attached; it can now be used on the grown cell.
reaction: The opposing centrosomes and microtubules make the spindle’s layout clear, though how it attaches to chromosomes remains to be shown.
reason: Use the spindle to form two daughter nuclei; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The spindle will separate sister chromatids so two nuclei can form, although the intermediate attachment steps are uncertain.

effect: The spindle step produced two nuclei with complete genomes, but the cytoplasm remains connected and must divide.
reaction: The distinction between nuclear and cytoplasmic division is clear, though chromosome attachment and separation were skipped.
reason: Use actin and myosin to divide the cytoplasm; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the cleavage furrow and separate the cell into two daughters.

effect: Cytoplasmic division produced two separate stem cells, each with a complete genome; the chapter’s goals are complete.
reaction: The final picture plan clearly distinguishes self-renewal from later differentiation, though it does not show how actin and myosin constrict the cell.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle and then dividing the cytoplasm was the most worthwhile sequence: it separated nuclear division from the formation of two cell bodies.

leastWorthwhile.text: The spindle result skipped chromosome attachment and separation, leaving a gap between its construction and two complete daughter nuclei.

surprise.text: The membrane supply appeared as vesicles beside an ER and Golgi inset, rather than as membrane added directly; fusion then enlarged the cell. The inset did not explain those organelles’ roles.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear goal, although the final steps were the only offered combinations, so they involved little choice rather than discovery of compatibility.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the daughter cells become different tissues, though I would want the next chapter to explain more of the intermediate mechanisms.
